text: Marketing spends money to reach people, and Salesforce records who was reached, who responded, and what followed. Let's use the standard campaign reports to answer those three questions.

Here is the standard Campaigns with Campaign Members report from Trailhead. Each row is one member, showing member status and whether they responded. It's only as good as those statuses being kept current. The report type you pick decides which fields you can use.

Campaigns gives one row per campaign, with statistics like cost and roll-up counts. Campaigns with Campaign Members covers reach and response. Campaigns with Opportunities links pipeline. Influenced Opportunities needs Campaign Influence, depending on edition and setup. Exact names vary by org, so browse the Campaigns category in your own report type picker.

Response rate is responded members divided by members reached. Use the campaign roll-up fields in a summary formula, or group members by campaign with the responded flag as a matrix column. Number sent is often manual, so verify it before you divide. If it doesn't exist, count members with a sent status and label the denominator as such.

Two cautions. Most orgs credit an opportunity to one primary campaign source, so a customer touched twice gives one campaign all the credit. And parent campaign roll-ups include their children, so listing both double counts. Decide whether you're reporting at program level or tactic level, and filter accordingly.
Response is measured. Now for the money. Next up: ROI reporting.
